A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temporal-wise distillation framework. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 contains proofs and experimental details in the main text; v2 relocates these to Appendices A–B and adds supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results on four datasets, objective ablations, loss and clustering visualizations, and evaluations across training and inference timesteps.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments measuring training costs, firing rates, additional architectures and confidence-based early exits.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(9) and Algorithm 1 retain the same temporal cross-entropy, teacher distillation and ensemble self-distillation objectives. Additional backbones, teacher-free ablations and application of SEENN-I evaluate the existing framework without revising its proposed training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and CIFAR10-DVS. The additional architecture and early-exit experiments use existing datasets and tasks; they change model configurations and inference procedures rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the direct-training comparator with standard logits-based distillation. v2 Table 7 adds logits-KD controls to the full-range comparison previously containing only proposed-method models in v1 Table 8. The comparator sets in the principal dataset benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Original splits, preprocessing, training budgets and hyperparameters are retained in Appendix B. Appendix C substantially broadens evaluation procedures through Spikingformer, MS-ResNet and VGGSNN configurations, time/memory and firing-rate measurements, and SEENN-I confidence thresholds from 0.7 to 0.999 with accuracy and average inference timesteps reported.

E4.justification: v2 adds a self-distillation-without-teacher ablation in Table 5, objective ablations on VGGSNN/CIFAR10-DVS, and explicit logits-KD controls for timestep robustness. Appendix C also adds training-overhead diagnostics, firing-rate analysis and an early-exit case study. These substantially extend the retained hyperparameter, loss and clustering analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three-run averaging for the CIFAR and CIFAR10-DVS benchmark tables. v2 introduces no new seed disclosures, uncertainty intervals, significance tests or repeated-run procedures. Its firing-rate means are measured outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing headline scores, including 71.04% on ImageNet, remain unchanged. New results include 78.94% and 79.63% for the teacher-free ablation, logits-KD full-range controls, and Appendix C measurements across costs, firing rates, architectures and early exits. Table 14 reports 79.05% at 1.690 average timesteps for the proposed T=6 model at confidence threshold 0.9.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, Propositions 2–3 and their derivations are retained. Appendix A relocates the proofs and repeats the existing statements as Equations (13)–(15); it does not introduce new assumptions, bounds or mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the claims of temporal-wise distillation, convergence across implicit timestep models, flexible deployment without timestep-specific retraining, and strong benchmark performance. The expanded evidence and more explicit logit-based title do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands practical interpretation: it distinguishes inference-budget flexibility from benefits of additional training resources and explains how timestep robustness supports early exits. Appendix C discusses transformer teacher-selection difficulties, temporal averaging weakening the DVS teacher, and potential feature-alignment problems with adaptive input encoders. These applicability considerations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability link in the abstract and measured per-batch training time and memory in Table 9. Existing software, hardware, optimizer, preprocessing and hyperparameter disclosures move to Appendix B without substantive changes. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly discusses Ding et al.'s adjacent-timestep ensemble distillation and distinguishes the present ensemble-to-submodel supervision. References to SEENN, additional architectures, recent transformers and adaptive encoding support the expanded discussion. The broader positioning around efficient logits-based SNN distillation remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document by moving proofs and the experimental-details subsection into Appendices A–B, adding Appendix C, and expanding the practical discussion. It also revises the title, adds acknowledgments and an impact statement, and adopts author–year citations. Much of the retained scientific prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds six appendix tables, expands the objective-ablation and full-range comparison tables, redraws Figure 1's baseline panel, and annotates the existing t-SNE plots with red boxes. The hyperparameter table moves to the appendix, and the document adopts ICML formatting with running headers and single-column appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central efficiency and deployment claims. The added matched logits-KD timestep controls, measured training overhead and SEENN-I accuracy–cost tradeoffs address important validation gaps in v1. Teacher-free ablations and additional architectures further test the framework's usefulness. These gains improve empirical credibility despite unchanged uncertainty reporting and limited implementation detail for some new experiments.
